meta.resultsSource: Rhode Island Board of Elections, Election Results (unofficial and partial), towns added up by county
meta.landSource: U.S. Census Bureau, 2020 Census Redistricting Data (P.L. 94-171), county land area (AREALAND)
meta.countyRow: counties[i] = [Democratic votes, Republican votes, all other votes, total votes] for meta.counties[i]
sources: Rhode Island Board of Elections, Election Results, Nov. 3, 2026 general election: unofficial results by city and town from the site's Media Export, as of Nov. 9, 2026, 2:31 PM ET, retrieved 2026-11-09, added up by county here. The State of Rhode Island's copyright policy says compiled information on its site is public information and may be distributed or copied, and asks for credit.
Partial: the site marks 90 of its 456 precincts "Partially Reported", so some ballots, such as provisional ballots, may still be added before the Board of Elections certifies the results.
Not on the map: 776 U.S. Senate votes on federal-only ballots, which the results list apart from any town. They are in the state's totals but in no county.

Left out: Governor, Helena Buonanno Foulkes (Democrat) 207,473, Kenneth Block (independent) 99,817, Aaron C. Guckian (Republican) 47,382, C. D. Reynolds (independent) 2,049, Jasjit S. Gotra (independent) 1,672; Secretary of State, Gregg M. Amore (Democrat) 275,425. In the Governor's race an independent finished second, which a map of a Democrat against a Republican can't show. U.S. House has two districts, so it isn't statewide. Ballot questions and local races aren't here either.

U.S. Census Bureau, 2020 Census Redistricting Data (P.L. 94-171): county land area and codes, which county each town is in, cities, and each block's location and adults, for placing dots within a county.

U.S. Census Bureau, 2020 TIGER/Line® Shapefiles, tabulation blocks: where people were counted, for keeping dots off empty land. TIGER/Line® is a registered trademark of the Census Bureau; the land grid here isn't a Census Bureau product.
U.S. Census Bureau, Cartographic Boundary Files, 2017 counties, via us-atlas v3.0.1 (counties-10m.json).
Software: three.js r160, d3-geo 3.1.1, topojson-client 3.1.0.
